extracted.intended_audience: Texas regulated entities, stakeholders, and members of the public who review and comment on TCEQ proposed rules (including environmental professionals and legal practitioners).
extracted.subtask_description: Information and procedural requirements for Texas Commission on Environmental Quality rule proposals published for public comment, including required metadata, documentation, comment submission method, and post-comment processing. Used by agencies, regulated parties, and public commenters to find, review, and submit comments on proposed rules.

rubrics_metrics.name: Proposal publication requirement
rubrics_metrics.description: Proposals are rules that have been approved by the commissioners to be published in the Texas Register for public comment.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: A proposal must be approved by the TCEQ commissioners and then published in the Texas Register to begin the public comment period; publication in the Register is the formal start of the notice-and-comment process.

rubrics_metrics.name: Public comment period length
rubrics_metrics.description: The public comment period usually lasts for 30 days after the publication date.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Expect approximately a 30-day window for submitting comments after publication; actual windows are shown per-proposal (e.g., 5/15/2026–6/15/2026).

rubrics_metrics.name: Post-comment evaluation and revision
rubrics_metrics.description: After the public comment period has closed, staff evaluates all comments and makes appropriate changes to the proposed rule.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: TCEQ staff review submitted comments and may revise the proposal accordingly before filing the draft adoption. Commenters should provide substantive, actionable input if they want it considered in revisions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Filing draft adoption with Chief Clerk / movement to Pending Adoptions
rubrics_metrics.description: The draft adoption is then filed with the Chief Clerk and moved to Pending Adoptions.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Once staff completes evaluation and any revisions, the proposal advances as a draft adoption via the Chief Clerk and appears in the Pending Adoptions list for further processing.

rubrics_metrics.name: Proposal date metadata (Approval Date & Comments Due)
rubrics_metrics.description: Each proposal listing shows Approval Date and Comments Due (e.g., Approval Date: 4/30/26; Comments Due: 6/16/26).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Listings must clearly present the approval date and the deadline for public comments so stakeholders know the official timelines.

rubrics_metrics.name: Submission method and comment window
rubrics_metrics.description: Submit via TCEQ Public Comments with an explicit submission window (displayed per-proposal, e.g., 5/15/2026–6/15/2026).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The page specifies the required submission channel (TCEQ Public Comments) and the exact open/close dates for submissions; commenters should use that channel and respect the stated window.

rubrics_metrics.name: Rule project identifier
rubrics_metrics.description: Each proposal includes a Rule Project Number (e.g., 2026-006-309-OW).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The project number is a unique identifier for tracking the rulemaking; include it in correspondence and comments to ensure accurate association.

rubrics_metrics.name: Short title / description
rubrics_metrics.description: Each proposal includes a Short Title/Description summarizing the subject (e.g., 'Land Application of Produced Water').
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Provide and display a concise title and brief description so readers can quickly determine relevance.

rubrics_metrics.name: Proposal document availability (PDF)
rubrics_metrics.description: Proposal (PDF) — downloadable proposal document is linked from the listing.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The full proposed rule text or proposal package should be available as a PDF for review; commenters rely on the PDF to prepare substantive comments.

rubrics_metrics.name: Executive summary inclusion
rubrics_metrics.description: Each listing links to an Executive Summary for the proposal.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: An executive summary is provided to explain the purpose, scope, and key elements of the proposal in a concise format for reviewers.

rubrics_metrics.name: Rule chapter references
rubrics_metrics.description: Proposals list the affected rule chapters (e.g., Ch. 210; Ch. 309; Ch. 114; Ch. 328; Ch. 37; Ch. 293).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Identify which parts of the Texas Administrative Code are amended or affected so stakeholders can locate existing provisions and assess impacts.

rubrics_metrics.name: Plain language summary and translations
rubrics_metrics.description: Some proposals provide a Plain Language Summary and Plain Language Summary (Spanish).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Provide plain-language explanations (and translations where applicable) to improve accessibility for non-technical audiences and non-English speakers.

rubrics_metrics.name: Statutory implementation / legislative authority
rubrics_metrics.description: Proposal descriptions state the statutory authority or legislative provisions being implemented (e.g., 'Amendment of Chapters 309 and 210 to implement SB 1145', 'This rulemaking implements House Bill (HB) 3229').
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Explicitly cite the enabling legislation or bill the rule implements so reviewers understand legal basis and legislative intent.

rubrics_metrics.name: Related actions / concurrent revisions
rubrics_metrics.description: Listings may note related or concurrent actions (e.g., 'It is associated with a concurrent I/M SIP revision (2026-004-SIP-NR)').
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Indicate linkages to other rulemakings or SIP revisions so commenters can consider cross-cutting effects and coordinate comments across related proceedings.
